question.problem:
The following table shows the speed $v$, in $\text{km/min},$ at certain times during a family car trip over a period of $60$ minutes.

| $t\,(\text{min})$ | $60$ | $70$ | $80$ | $95$ | $110$ | $120$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v\,(\text{km/min})$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1.5$ |

Assuming that the family traveled $130\,\text{km}$ during the first hour of the trip, use the left Riemann sum to approximate the total distance traveled during the first two hours.

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the speed-time graph.*
question.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=5$ rectangles. Using the left Riemann sum, the area is approximated as

$$
A≈v(60)Δ{t}_{1}+v(70)Δ{t}_{2}+v(80)Δ{t}_{3}+v(95)Δ{t}_{4}+v(110)Δ{t}_{5},
$$

where each $Δ{t}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $t$-value and the next one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{t}_{i}={t}_{i+1}-{t}_{i}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δt$'s.

| $t$ | $60$ | $70$ | $80$ | $95$ | $110$ | $120$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δt$ | $10$ | $10$ | $15$ | $15$ | $10$ | $-$ |
| $v(t)$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1.5$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈10\cdot 1.5+10\cdot 2+15\cdot 1+15\cdot 1+10\cdot 2 \\  & =15+20+15+15+20 \\  & =85\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

In the given context, the area under the curve represents the distance covered in $60$ minutes of travel, from $t=60$ minutes to $t=120$ minutes. The distance traveled in the first two hours is 

$$
\begin{aligned}d=130+85=215\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$
